title: Container Bookings: Amount of the Change-of-Destination Fee
content:
This page fixes how the Container Bookings change-of-destination fee is priced once the chargeable containers are known.

## Rule

The fee for a change still owing is the product's change-of-destination rate per container multiplied by the chargeable containers. The multiplication is carried out in full and the product of it is rounded to two decimal places once, at the very end. Each change still owing receives its own fee entry. The free amendment allowance has no bearing on this fee: the fee is due whatever amount of the allowance remains, and the change nevertheless continues to count towards that allowance. Where no change is owing, the fee is zero and nothing is booked.

## Worked example (hypothetical rate)

Take an invented rate of 312.50 per container and 7 chargeable containers: the fee is 2187.50. Take instead an invented rate of 100.004 per container and 5 chargeable containers: the full product is 500.02, and that is the fee, because rounding happens only on the final figure and never on the rate. Neither rate is a real product rate.

## Points of judgement

- **Two changes owing:** two separate entries, each priced on the same basis.
- **Allowance exhausted or not:** makes no difference to the amount.
- **Zero chargeable containers:** the fee is 0.00 and no entry is made.
